controls.control: Service credential scope is compared against signed claims
Local private API derives workspace and project scope
Durable records carry explicit workspace scope at the database layer
Portable export secret references carry no workspace scope
Local filesystem/project operations require a current LocalProjectGrant
Canonical path containment for filesystem/project operations
Runtime Gateway node identity is operator-signed and verified against durable records
controls.note: The gateway service verifies only. The repository also ships an issuer CLI (CP190-F16).

controls.control: Runtime Gateway commands are workspace/node/generation bound on every frame
Remote command expiry is bounded to 24 hours
Direct-local execution cannot bypass Control Plane policy because components are co-located
Native external sessions are listed as scoped opaque references
Remote-control interaction responses are principal-checked
Tool invocation requires a matching grant, policy decision, approval and rate limit
Accepted plan tool grants are cross-checked at invocation time
Model credentials are supplied as a separate credential reference, never as model context
Provider output is untrusted data that cannot widen caller authority
Artifact keys are content-addressed and the store root is canonical-pinned
Sandbox outputs become artifacts only through an authorised promotion gate
Local backups and portable exports exclude protected secret material
Administrative routes require a scoped service credential of the service class
The control plane composes a deny-by-default policy decision point
Deployed public ingress is bounded against request floods

auditAreas.area: remote Runtime Gateway versus product relay
HPKE AAD, recipient, replay and expiry
auditAreas.notes: RFC 9180 DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256)/HKDF-SHA256/AES-128-GCM; AAD binds version, suite, key id, workspace, host, command id, payload type and schema, issued/expiry and content digest; 1 MiB cap; wrong recipient, tamper, downgrade and digest mismatch all fail closed.

Frozen lockfile with integrity hashes, digest-pinned base images and actions, pinned patched dependency with upstream provenance, Trivy image scan with CycloneDX SBOM, build provenance attestation, least-privilege workflow permissions, persist-credentials disabled, pull_request_target workflows never check out PR code.

findings.title: Product relay metadata-only commands are unauthenticated
findings.releaseImpact: Blocks any remote-control acceptance for the Local and Hosted profiles. Whole-cloud trust acceptance stays held.
findings.routedTo: W1 (packages/remote-control-relay) with the Agent HQ product relay owner
findings.regression: A relay metadata command must carry an authenticated envelope or a request signature bound to the host key. Regression test: reject a metadata command with no authentication field, and reject a forged approve/deny/cancel for a known targetId.

findings.title: Relay effects are applied before the durable idempotency receipt, and no durable receipt implementation ships
findings.releaseImpact: Duplicate live effects on any relay redelivery or host restart. Blocks STA-L16-01 and STA-L78-01 acceptance.
findings.regression: Write the idempotency receipt before the effect and make the receipt durable. Regression test: with a receipt store whose write fails, assert the effect did not run; and after a restart, assert a replayed envelope is rejected as duplicate.

findings.title: LocalProjectGrant is not enforced on the direct-local path and the production discovery state is a hard-coded constant
findings.releaseImpact: The Control Plane cannot demonstrate STA-L17-01, STA-L42-09, STA-L42-10 or STA-L69-02. Local filesystem/project acceptance stays open.
findings.routedTo: W1 (runtime composition and adapter boundary) with the Agent HQ desktop grant owner
findings.regression: The direct-local driver must require a current grant and must contain every path against a canonical grant root after symlink resolution. Regression test: a direct-local dispatch with a revoked or absent grant is rejected, and a symlinked path escaping the grant root is rejected.

findings.title: The credential-vault egress guard does not see a secret inside a non-plain carrier
findings.releaseImpact: A leased secret can leave the vault inside an Error, Map, Set or Buffer. Blocks STA-L40-17 and STA-L76-03 acceptance.
findings.regression: Extend the egress guard to traverse Error message/stack/cause, Map, Set, Buffer and typed arrays, or reject any non-plain result. Regression test: a leased operation returning new Error(secret) must raise SECRET_EGRESS_BLOCKED.

findings.title: The Local private API derives workspace and project scope from the request body
findings.releaseImpact: Any holder of the local bearer token can name another workspace. Cross-workspace fail-closed acceptance for the Local profile stays open.
findings.regression: Bind the Local principal to an authorized workspace and project set and compare the envelope against it. Regression test: a valid local token with a foreign workspaceId must be rejected.

findings.title: Log, event and checkpoint redaction is key-name based and misses compound credential key names
findings.releaseImpact: A secret stored under a key such as sessionToken is written to logs and events. STA-L76-03 acceptance stays open.
findings.regression: Extend the sensitive key set to compound credential names, or apply the production value-based canary guard at every sink. Regression test: a secret under sessionToken, passphrase or bearerToken must not appear in a redacted log payload.

findings.title: Runtime Gateway runtime commands are not bounded to the 24 hour remote-command maximum
findings.releaseImpact: A runtime command stays dispatchable for an unbounded lifetime and survives credential rotation. STA-L61-08 acceptance stays open.
findings.regression: Apply the same 24 hour bound to the runtime command family. Regression test: enqueuing a runtime command with a one-year lifetime must fail with EXPIRY_TOO_LONG.

findings.title: A Local filesystem checkpoint copies the private-file secrets directory in cleartext
findings.releaseImpact: Operator backups carry plaintext provider secrets. STA-L76-01 and STA-L76-03 acceptance stay open for the Local profile.
findings.regression: Exclude the secrets directory from the checkpoint inventory or seal it under the vault key. Regression test: a checkpoint of a data directory containing secrets/provider-key must not contain the secret bytes.

findings.title: SQLite WAL and SHM sidecars keep the pre-restriction file mode
findings.releaseImpact: On a relaxed data directory the sidecars that hold recent writes are group and world readable. STA-L76-01 acceptance stays open.
findings.regression: Restrict the sidecar files to owner-only as well. Regression test: after opening a provider in a 0755 directory the -wal and -shm files must be mode 0600.

findings.title: The portable import path scans with an empty sensitive-value list and portable secret references are not workspace scoped
findings.releaseImpact: A profile export can carry another workspace's secret locator, and the import path does not re-check secret values. STA-L08-01 and STA-L76-03 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Scan the import path with the same sensitive values used at export and scope secret references to a workspace. Regression test: a manifest whose record value carries a secret under a non-prohibited key must be rejected on import.

findings.title: Sandbox credential bindings are injected after the ambient-credential denial runs
findings.releaseImpact: The ambient credential denial never sees credential-bound names, so a raw secret reaches the sandbox environment. STA-L77-01 acceptance stays open.
findings.regression: Apply the ambient credential denial to the effective environment, including credential bindings, or deny any credential-shaped bound name. Regression test: a credential bound to AWS_SESSION must be denied or must not reach the provider environment.

findings.title: The sandbox metadata-service deny list is incomplete
findings.releaseImpact: Non-default cloud metadata endpoints are reachable from a sandbox command. STA-L77-01 acceptance stays open.
findings.regression: Deny the link-local metadata range and the known provider metadata endpoints. Regression test: a command targeting 169.254.170.2 must be denied with POLICY_DENIED.

findings.title: The sandbox provider contract is not composed into any application and no live provider exists
findings.releaseImpact: There is no sandbox boundary in any shipped profile. STA-L77-01 and STA-L83-02 acceptance stay open and the live E2B gate remains unproven.
findings.routedTo: W1 (profile composition) and the operations owner for the E2B template and cleanup thresholds
findings.regression: Compose a SandboxProvider in the hosted profile and record the live template, resource, network and cleanup evidence. Regression test: a hosted composition must resolve a sandbox provider, and a composition without one must fail closed.

findings.title: The only public control-plane service has no HTTP request rate limit and no inbound deadline
findings.releaseImpact: An authenticated principal can saturate the PostgreSQL pool. Abuse-boundary acceptance for the cloud profile stays open.
findings.routedTo: W1 (apps/control-api) with the operations owner for the deployed limit values
findings.regression: Add a per-principal request quota and an inbound request deadline to the Fastify adapter. Regression test: a principal exceeding the quota receives a bounded 429 without reaching the database.

findings.title: The Restate ingress submission carries no request credential
findings.releaseImpact: Workflow submission trusts network placement only. STA-L24-01 and STA-L40-09 acceptance stay open for the self-hosted profile, where the ingress binds to all interfaces.
findings.routedTo: W1 (execution acceptance) and the deployment owner for the self-hosted ingress binding
findings.regression: Authenticate the ingress submission with the Restate request identity, and bind the self-hosted ingress to the private interface. Regression test: a submission without the request identity must be rejected.

findings.title: The Control Plane repository ships a RuntimeNode credential issuer
findings.releaseImpact: The operator issuer private key lives on Control Plane infrastructure. Credential-class separation and rotation acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Move issuance to a separate operator-controlled surface and keep the gateway verifier-only. Regression test: the Control Plane image must not contain an issuer private key path.

findings.title: The synthetic RuntimeNode authority merges credential classes and drops the binding fence
findings.releaseImpact: Gateway authentication tests do not exercise the production issuer and device separation. STA-L46-01 and STA-L46-04 acceptance rest on code reading, not on the test suite.
findings.regression: Give the synthetic authority a distinct issuer key and enforce the node, workspace and generation fence. Regression test: a device-signed credential presented with an issuer key id must be rejected, and a consumed credential for another workspace must be refused.

findings.title: The pi-durable tool path does not cross-check the accepted plan tool grants
findings.releaseImpact: A tool call can present a self-consistent grant for a tool and operation the accepted plan does not grant. STA-L42-01 and STA-L42-07 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Cross-check the accepted plan constraints.tools.grants on the pi-durable path. Regression test: a grant for a tool absent from the accepted plan must be denied.

findings.title: No policy decision point is composed into any application, so the credential lease positive path does not exist
findings.releaseImpact: The deny-by-default behaviour is proven, but the narrowly authorized executor path in STA-L40-18 cannot be demonstrated in this repository.
findings.routedTo: W1 (profile compositions) and the Cedar policy owner
findings.regression: Compose the decision point where a credential lease is required and record the permit matrix. Regression test: a leased connector credential in a composed profile must be allowed only for its own workspace and operation.

findings.title: Provider contributions and ProjectState items carry free-form content with no secret filter and no untrusted-data marking
findings.releaseImpact: A provider or retrieved memory value can carry a credential into a ContextPackage, a ProjectState item or model context. STA-L40-17 and STA-L54-12 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Filter provider and ProjectState content against the protected value set and mark retrieved content as untrusted data. Regression test: a contribution whose content carries a canary must be rejected or redacted before admission.

findings.title: The environment and private-file secret providers ignore the SecretUse context
findings.releaseImpact: A secret resolved through the env or file provider is not bound to a workspace, operation or purpose. STA-L40-18 and STA-L42-08 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Accept and enforce the SecretUse context in every provider. Regression test: resolving the same reference under two different use contexts must not produce the same unbound lease.

findings.title: The Hosted server profile composes no credential vault and the host-secure handle provider has no resolver
findings.releaseImpact: The self-hosted server profile has no dynamic credential lifecycle and no OS-secure handle path. STA-L15-01, STA-L40-11 and STA-L40-14 acceptance stay open.
findings.routedTo: W1 (apps/hosted-control-plane composition) and the desktop owner for the OS resolver
findings.regression: Compose the vault for the hosted server profile and wire a concrete host-secure resolver for packaged Local. Regression test: a hosted server composition must resolve a credential lifecycle, and a packaged Local profile must resolve an opaque handle.

findings.title: The spawn policy check is not pinned to the executed path
findings.releaseImpact: A symlink swap between the allowlist check and the spawn can launch an unlisted executable. STA-L69-01 and STA-L77-01 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Execute the resolved canonical path and re-verify the device and inode identity, as the secrets provider already does. Regression test: swapping the allowlisted executable for a symlink after the check must not launch the replacement.

findings.title: The exported direct-local ACP runtime factory applies no spawn policy by default
findings.releaseImpact: An embedder can start an arbitrary absolute executable at an arbitrary absolute working directory. STA-L27-03 and STA-L77-01 acceptance stay open for embedders.
findings.regression: Require an explicit spawn policy in the exported factory. Regression test: creating the factory without a spawn policy must fail closed.

findings.title: Marketplace registry egress accepts any HTTPS URL with no metadata-range denial
findings.releaseImpact: A misconfigured registry base URL can reach a metadata endpoint. STA-L31-02 and STA-L33-01 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Deny the link-local and metadata ranges on the registry fetch path. Regression test: a registry base URL resolving to 169.254.169.254 must be refused.

findings.title: The Restate interaction response handler resolves by name without a responding-principal check
findings.releaseImpact: An approval or input delivered over the workflow ingress is not re-checked against the authorized principal set on that path. STA-L66-01 and STA-L42-11 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Re-check the responding principal against the interaction allowed principal set before resolving. Regression test: a response from a principal outside allowedPrincipalIds must be rejected.

findings.title: Tool rate-limit events are only deleted for the tuple being checked
findings.releaseImpact: Rows for abandoned principal, tool or operation tuples accumulate without bound. Retention acceptance stays open.
findings.regression: Sweep expired tool rate-limit rows in the retention pass. Regression test: the retention sweep must remove expired tool_rate_limit_events rows for a tuple that is never called again.

findings.title: Staging and production share one R2 bucket credential slot and are separated by a key prefix only
findings.releaseImpact: The asserted environment credential separation is a naming convention, not an enforced control. STA-L31-01, STA-L31-02 and STA-L40-11 acceptance stay open.
findings.regression: Provision distinct bucket-scoped R2 credentials per environment. Regression test: the production credential must not read a staging object and the staging credential must not read a production object.

openGates: No permitted live profile evidence exists for the managed cloud, Local, or self-hosted profiles, so whole-cloud and whole-runtime trust acceptance stays held.

Agent HQ owns LocalProjectGrant issuance, desktop key storage, Event Gateway authorization, durable ContentSyncDevice and ContentKeyEpoch flows, and the product relay credential; none of those controls can be closed from this repository.
No live E2B sandbox provider, template, cleanup threshold or credential-denial evidence exists.
No live managed-cloud vault rotation and restore evidence exists for the selected credential-vault provider.
Packaged Local OS-secure handle resolution and packaged binary signing evidence remain absent.
Malware scanner composition, quarantine and fail-closed outage evidence remain a product-owned gate.
The independent human penetration review required by the issue acceptance criteria has not been performed; the probes in this lane are credential-free synthetic evidence only.
This reviewer approves none of the routed fixes; each routed owner must verify its own fix on its own exact head and an independent reviewer must then re-verify.
